title: Defeater-search saturation stopping surrogate
question: When repeated adversarial search stops finding new defeater classes, when is it reasonable to pause rather than recurse forever?

model.assumption: Comparable rounds are modeled as Bernoulli/iid-like opportunities to discover at least one new defeater class.
model.observation: k consecutive rounds discover zero new classes.
model.meaning: one-sided upper bound on the per-round probability of discovering a new class under the declared surrogate

invariants: No finite adversarial search proves completeness.
A stopping rule should state what residual novelty rate it is willing to tolerate.
Stopping defeater search is a resource decision, not proof that unknown failures do not exist.
New evidence or a new failure mode resets the saturation argument.
boundary: Search rounds are rarely truly iid or equally powerful; this is a transparent stopping surrogate, not a completeness theorem.
